summary: The PR removes a guard check for `user.address` in `getUserCity`, introducing a regression where passing a user object without an address will throw a runtime `TypeError` instead of returning `null`.

findings.title: Unsafe property access causes runtime TypeError when address is missing
findings.description: Removing the `if (!user.address)` guard check causes `getUserCity` to attempt reading `user.address.city` directly. If `user.address` is `undefined` or `null`, this will throw a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')` instead of handling missing addresses gracefully.
findings.verificationHypothesis: If `getUserCity({ name: 'Alice' })` or `getUserCity({ address: null })` is called, the function will throw a TypeError instead of returning `null`.

suggestedReproduction.preconditions: User object is provided without an `address` property or with `address` set to `null` or `undefined`.
suggestedReproduction.expectedBehavior: The function returns `null` or `undefined` without throwing an error.
suggestedReproduction.suspiciousBehavior: The function throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'city')`.
